prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1040; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a left-turn collision at an intersection, with the insured's vehicle struck while the claimant was turning across oncoming traffic. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will route through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the photos taken at the scene. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's account, and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and the collision occurred as described.

Entry 3: Inspected the vehicle with the appraiser. The damage pattern lines up with the impact described, and the repair estimate reflects only what this collision would produce.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file points to prior damage to this vehicle, and the prior-loss history is clean.

Entry 5: Received the initial medical report documenting whiplash. The injury is consistent with the mechanism of a side impact of this kind, and the claimant has no record of prior complaints involving the same area of the body.

Entry 6: Treatment began with a physical therapy plan and followed the usual course for soft-tissue neck injuries. Notes show steady improvement, and visit frequency has tapered as the claimant's symptoms eased.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the treatment records. The account given to the attorney matches what the claimant told me in our earlier calls, with no changes to the sequence or the description of the collision.

Entry 8: Reviewed the file with the supervisor. All sources agree on how the accident occurred and on the claimant's presence in the vehicle, and the medical course and vehicle damage fit the reported loss. Claim remains open pending final treatment summary.
